role: calibration only: Siegel-zero scenario, i.e. would a tiny L(1,χ_{−4p}) starve Type II / (★)?

M_BM = M₀ − T with T ∝ L(1,χ_p)² (BM_LVALUE Thm A), and unconditionally M_BM(p) ≥ 0.9225·M₀(p) at p ≡ 1 (8) and ≥ M₀ − o(1) at p ≡ 5 (8) (Stephens). A Siegel discriminant −4p only changes small-prime residue patterns. Apparent h(−4p) effects among (★)-zeros are the p ≡ 1 (3) conditioning artefact (out_Q06 Z0803). Fluctuations below the main term are the open part (H⁻_BM).
status_ref: BM_LVALUE.md Thm A + 0.9225·M₀ bound; out_Q06 Z0803 (scripts/z52d_avenue_Q06_hzeros.py); BRAINSTORM/hardness_law.md

The data favour order N log²N, and this is now an internal theorem for Type I: Σ_{p≤N} f_I(p) ≪ N log²N unconditionally ((D)32b, PROVED relative to Kuznetsov/Petersson, Weil, Selberg 3/16; needs external scrutiny). This removes ET's log log N. The slow decrease is a lower-order term (c + d/log N). Average statement (B6).

role: calibration only: Σ_{n≤N} f(n) over all n outgrows N log³N
missing_theorem: (Calibration; heuristic explanation.) Over composites, f(n) includes solutions inherited from every divisor d | n by scaling, so Σ_{n≤N} f(n) ≳ Σ_d f_{I,II}(d)·N/d ≈ N Σ_d log³d/d ≍ N log⁴N heuristically. A growing ratio to N log³N is then expected. ET's log³ average refers to Type I/II-type counts. No proof role.
status_ref: FRONTIER §1 Counts (ET: average of f(n) ≍ log³n, which needs the precise definition of f); Pass 1 U03
next: Check ET's exact definition of f(n) for composite n before fitting. If it includes inherited solutions, the log exponent should be 4.

role: smooth auxiliary values: pick C with 4Cp+1 smooth and let many small prime classes cover −1 (Davenport/Erdős–Rényi template)
missing_theorem: For every p there is C ≤ X(p) such that 4Cp+1 is y-smooth and its prime-factor classes in (ℤ/4C)^× have −1 among their subset products. Smoothness raises the success rate (Pass 1: ×4, through more divisors). But no number of prime factors forces −1: all primes ≡ 1 (mod 4C) is always possible, and Davenport/Olson constants force the product 1, not −1. So the class condition (B2) survives intact. Davenport forcing is a recorded board dead end.

missing_theorem: A selector choosing which ET family certifies p is a Chebotarev (Frobenius) condition in a fixed finite Galois extension, and the selected families always succeed. This is false: fixed finite Frobenius data are inert on finite witness sets ((J)96), and any bounded procedure fails i.o. under H (B1 Thm C). Pass 1 found only the known mod-840 class effect.

role: arcsine (Deshouillers–Dress–Tenenbaum) law for class-restricted divisors of 4Cp+1
missing_theorem: A tied-modulus DDT law at fixed p (the divisors of 4Cp+1 in class −1 mod 4C, over C, have a limiting log-distribution with no atom at 'none') would give existence. Feng (2021) proves residue-class DDT only as a Cesàro mean over n at a fixed modulus (B6). Pass 1: certificate divisors have a tent law peaked at log d/log N = 1/2, not arcsine, because both d and N/d must be ≥ 4C − 1. A pointwise class-restricted version is the B2 event.
status_ref: Pass 1 H03 (Feng hal-03216035; 300 primes near 10⁶); FRONTIER §3 B6, B2

role: analytic continuation / functional equation ('loop equation') for F(s) = Σ f(n) n^{−s}, then Perron
missing_theorem: F(s) has a continuation with enough structure that Perron's formula with explicit kernels yields f(n) ≥ 1 pointwise. Perron gives partial sums. Isolating one coefficient needs F on a vertical segment of height ≫ n, which encodes the coefficient itself. Dirichlet-series/Euler-product hardness laws are a recorded dead end (averages, B6). No functional equation is expected: f is not multiplicative, and the Type I/II conditions have tied moduli.
status_ref: FRONTIER §6 'Dirichlet series / moments / Euler-product hardness laws → averages (B6)'; BRAINSTORM/anal_dirichlet_series.md

missing_theorem: For some K, the constraints 'no certificate of modulus ≤ K' are inconsistent with p prime ≡ 1 (24), viewed through residues of p mod small moduli. False: the avoider density δ*(T) is positive at every T because the square class survives (Mordell–Schinzel; B1 Thm M: the formal run at the square-mimicking point is consistent). Pass 1: −log δ* ≍ (log T)^{2.3–2.6}, bounded by T^{1/3+o(1)}. Propagating QR constraints adds only parity (CLASS_FORCING).
status_ref: DISCOVERIES (H)7, (H)10; POINTWISE_OMEGA Thm 9.3; B1 Thm M; Pass 1 H03 (covered)

role: second moment plus alterations on an explicit structured subfamily of hard primes
missing_theorem: For an explicit infinite family 𝓕 of Mordell-hard primes (e.g. p ≡ 1 (840) with 5 | 4p+1), f(p) ≥ 1 for every p ∈ 𝓕, by a variance bound. Second-moment arguments give a positive proportion of 𝓕 (B6), not every member. A congruence-defined 𝓕 in a square class contains sterile points, so infinitely many members defeat any bounded certificate menu under H (B1 Thm C). Pass 1: the subset's high P(S₁) (0.73) is the fixed-class effect 5 | 4p+1 (level C = 1 gets a factor 5 ≡ 1 mod 4, which does not help by itself). No signal at C = 100.
status_ref: FRONTIER §3 B1 (Thm C, CONDITIONAL on H), B6; §6 'Fixed-p variance … → critical'; Pass 1 U03

role: Linnik for shifted multiples: every p has some C with a PRIME factor q ≡ −1 (mod 4C) of 4Cp+1
missing_theorem: For every p, ∃C, ∃ prime q ≡ −1 (mod 4C) with q | 4Cp+1. Pass 1 (PROVED): this holds iff q = 4uC − 1 is prime with q | p + u, i.e. the (★) triples with prime witness modulus. Measured mean count ≈ 0.55 log p (vs R ≈ 0.165 log²p), and ≈ 0.8 % of primes near 10⁵, 10⁶ have none. A Poisson heuristic with mean 0.55 log p predicts ≈ x^{0.45} failures up to x. So the missing theorem is expected to be FALSE infinitely often: a thinner lottery than (★), heuristically subcritical.
status_ref: Pass 1 H03 (identity, PROVED; numerics at 10⁵–10⁷); FRONTIER §2.1
next: Close. A census of 'no prime-witness certificate' primes to 10⁷ would confirm growth like x^{0.45} (falsifying the statement on evidence).
note: Heuristic falsification. Prime-only witnesses are subcritical (mean ≍ log p, not log²p).

Class-free counts are provable pointwise: the I3 class-free count is ≥ c log²n at every n (PROVED, FRONTIER §7.17). τ in APs mod q ≍ p is classical for ranges x ≥ q^{3/2−δ} (Friedlander–Iwaniec / Heath-Brown τ₃-type results).
